description: ffmpeg is invoked with the global overwrite flag `-y` placed after the output filename, which makes ffmpeg interpret `-y` as a second output file (positional), causing the command to fail or behave unexpectedly. `-y` must appear before any output file arguments.

locations.section: process_video(): ffmpeg cmd list ends with output_path then "-y"

description: Combined removal segments are only concatenated and sorted; overlaps/adjacent segments are not merged and durations are not recomputed. This can create overlapping/duplicate removals, double-count removed duration, and later break video cutting logic that assumes non-overlap.

locations.section: combine_segments(): appends segments then only sorts; total_duration sums raw durations

description: Video processing assumes removal segments are clean (sorted, non-overlapping, within duration). It does not merge/clip/validate segments before computing keep intervals, so overlapping or out-of-range segments can produce incorrect keep segments (gaps lost, negative/zero-length keeps) and incorrect removed_duration (double-counting).

locations.section: main(): removed_duration = sum(s["duration"] for s in remove_segments) (assumes no overlaps)
calculate_keep_segments(): builds keep intervals without overlap/ordering validation or clipping to [0,total_duration]

description: If the removal segments cover the full timeline (or validation yields no keep segments), the ffmpeg filter builder will generate concat filters with n=0, which is invalid and will crash instead of producing a graceful empty/no-op output.

Pause/silence timestamps are treated as array indices (seconds) regardless of the energy window size. Since energy-calculator supports non-1.0 `--window-seconds`, detectors can output incorrect start/end times (off by a factor of window_seconds) and therefore cut the wrong parts of the video.

locations.section: detect_pauses(): uses index i as time in seconds; start_time interpreted as index
main()/detect_initial_silence(): returns silence_end as an index treated as seconds; ignores energy_data["window_seconds"]

description: Initial silence detection uses a moving average with convolution mode="valid" but does not compensate for the resulting index offset (smoothed series is shorter). The returned silence_end index is therefore systematically misaligned with the original timeline (up to smoothing_window-1 seconds), producing inaccurate cut boundaries.

locations.section: detect_initial_silence(): np.convolve(..., mode="valid") then uses loop index i directly as silence_end
